content.text: {"spec_patch":{"sense":{"what":["air temperature inside the fridge","relative humidity inside the fridge"],"interval_s":900},"environment":{"location":"inside a household refrigerator compartment","flags":["needs-airflow","temp:-15..70C","li-ion","rf-radiator"]},"power":{"source":"battery","target_life_days":90},"capabilities":["read.temperature_c","read.humidity_pct","net.wifi","power.battery"],"assumptions":["Runs on a rechargeable battery you can take out and recharge","Battery target is about 90 days between charges","Readings every 15 minutes instead of 5, to stretch battery life","Wi-Fi is used so alerts reach your phone","History is kept so you can see trends over time","Cold fridge temperatures are treated as normal operating conditions, not an alert"],"open_questions":[]},"candidate_questions":[],"assumptions":["Runs on a rechargeable battery you can take out and recharge","Battery target is about 90 days between charges","Readings every 15 minutes instead of 5, to stretch battery life"],"reply":"Battery it is — I'm designing around roughly three months between charges. To get there I've stretched the check interval from 5 minutes to 15, which is still plenty quick to catch a fridge warming up; say the word if you'd rather have faster readings and shorter battery life. Alerts still go to your phone over Wi-Fi when temperature or humidity drifts out of range, with history you can scroll back through. One thing worth flagging: Wi-Fi is the hungry part here, so a few months is ambitious and the final design will tell us how close we get."}
